open_obligations: Note that Buhl et al. state a requirement, not a proof that debate tolerates bounded systematic error.
Check whether 'washes out over training' corresponds to Brown-Cohen et al.'s stochastic-oracle Theorem 6.2.
Check how systematic error would be measured.
out.other_title: Open: debate with a flawed human-judgement oracle that errs on some queries
out.rationale: Brown-Cohen et al. ask whether debate results extend to oracles that err on some queries. Buhl et al. argue random judge errors should wash out over training, so the concern is systematic error, and require bounded systematic error of simulated human input with respect to reality and of the simulation with respect to humans; this is a stated requirement in a safety-case sketch, not a theorem.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: which kinds of human-judge error debate must tolerate, in a debate-based alignment safety case

text: The authors require that simulated human judges are competent at assessing debate outcomes; random errors should wash out over training, so the concern is systematic error, for example from claims playing on human biases or emotions. This needs two claims: the simulated human input has bounded systematic error with respect to reality, and the simulation has bounded systematic error with respect to the human input.
title: Good human input: bounded systematic error of human judges and their simulation
